sentences.text: -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:11489  MFA No. 100332 of 2022  ORAL JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by the judgment & award dated 03.03.2020 passed in MVC No.82/2017 on the file of the MACT., Gadag (for short, 'Tribunal').

3. Heard.
4.

Learned counsel Sri.Siddappa Sajjan appearing for the appellant-claimant would submit that the Tribunal committed an error in assessing the income, disability and awarded meager compensation on all other heads.
Thus, he seeks for reassessment of the compensation amount appropriately by allowing the appeal.

5. Per contra, learned counsel Sri.S.C.Bhuti appearing for the respondent-Corporation supporting the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal submits that in the absence of cogent and documentary evidence, the Tribunal has NC: 2024:KHC-D:11489 rightly assessed monthly income of the claimant at Rs.7,000/- per month, which is just and proper and needs no interference.
Further, he submits that as the PW2 is not a treated Doctor the disability assessed by the Tribunal is just and proper, does not call for modification.
He further submits that the award of compensation by the Tribunal on all heads is just and proper, does not call for interference.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.
6. I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and meticulously perused the appeal papers along with material available on record.
7. The pleading and evidence available on record indicates that the appellant-claimant sustained grievous injuries in a road accident dated 23.06.2016.

The appellant has sustained following injuries:
"*Fracture of latest condoyle right femur *Fracture of right fibula head & *Patella subluxation"
Shivappa S/O Fakkirappa Abbigeri vs The Managing Director on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52687913/
2 8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Taking note of the said injuries and considering the oral testimony of PW2 and other medical evidence available on NC: 2024:KHC-D:11489 record, I am of the considered view that it would be just and proper to re-assess disability at 13% for the purpose of determination of compensation.

Admittedly, the appellant has not placed any cogent and acceptable evidence with regard to his income, hence, I am of the considered view that it would be just and appropriate to re-assess the income of the claimant notionally relying on the notional income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Thus, relying on the above said chart, it would be appropriate to reassess the notional income of the claimant at Rs.8,750/- per month as the accident is of the year 2016.
9. There is no dispute with regard to the application of multiplier as 11.

Thus, loss of future income due to disability is recomputed as under:
Rs.8,750 (income) x 12(months) x 11(multiplier) x 13% (disability) = Rs.1,50,150/-
10.

Taking note of the oral testimony of PW2 and other evidence available on record, this Court re-assesses the compensation as under:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:11489 HEADS AMOUNT (in Rs.) Towards pain and suffering 50,000/- Towards Medical expenses 4,000/- Towards future medical expenses 10,000/- Diet, nourishment, conveyance and 20,000/- attendant charges Loss of income during laid-up period 26,250/- (Rs.8,750 X 3 months)

Loss of future earnings due to disability 1,50,150/-
Loss of amenities 30,000/-

Thus, the claimant shall be entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,90,400/- as against Rs.1,97,500/-
awarded by the learned Tribunal.

12. In the result, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,90,400/- as against Rs.1,97,500/-

3 awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: NC: 2024:KHC-D:11489 c) The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.
d) The respondent-Corporation shall deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from today.
e) On such deposit, the same shall be released in favour of the appellant/claimant.
f) Registry to transmit the records, if any, forthwith to the Tribunal.
g) Draw modified award accordingly.
